Alex — thanks for the telemetry, that helps. A few follow-ups so we size conservatively and avoid hot-path surprises: 

1) Quick computed baseline and peak tokens/sec (ballpark from what you sent):
   - Baseline: 120 QPS * 60 tokens = ~7,200 tokens/sec sustained.
   - Peak instantaneous (single-second): 2,800 QPS * 60 tokens = ~168,000 tokens/sec (short windows ~20–30s).
   - Long-form tail: when 400-token requests occur they increase instantaneous load but they are <2% of requests.

2) Implications for serving:
   - Continuous batching will help steady-state, but burst spikes will require headroom and fast autoscale/burst pools.
   - Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (checkout flows) could reduce token work significantly — please confirm reuse rate for identical prompts in your dataset.
   - Streaming chunk frequency (150–250 ms) means we need to optimize small-token emission latency (kernel choice + low-latency IO path). p95 chunk emission target <=200 ms is feasible but depends on model size & batch packing.

3) Initial sizing suggestion for trial (rough):
   - Start: 4 x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent) for baseline + canary (cover 120–500 QPS comfortably).
   - Promo burst plan: reserved burst pool of ~32 GPU-equivalents (or autoscale to that level with reserved burst capacity) to cover instantaneous token/sec peaks. Exact GPU count depends on model quantization and batch packing; we will calibrate with an internal perf test.

4) Data we still need from you:
   - A 15-minute high-resolution capture of a promo run (per-second QPS and average tokens).
   - Any backoff/retry behavior in your client (helps us model tail latencies).

I'll produce a short calc sheet and three sizing scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic) for Priya and Ben by Tue EOD PT.
